Let me verify the nginx conf, then do a clean consistent reset:

`resolveDevServerPorts(stateDir)`: For each dev server name, it reads the stored port, and if the stored port is available (isPortFree) it reuses it, otherwise it allocates a new one. When I started `just serve --apps=cms` (the second run), the stored ports were app:43189, cms:41487, boards:37315.

Wait, actually — when I started `just serve --apps=boards` (45394), resolveDevServerPorts was run: boards' stored port 37315... should be available (I had killed the reproduction). Hmm, but then boards was using 37315 (the banner was 37315? The boards.log I looked at earlier had 37315 in it).

Then `just serve --apps=cms` (50053): it ran resolveDevServerPorts for all 3 (always resolves all DEV_SERVERS). The stored ports at that point: app:43189, cms:41487, boards:37315.

- app: stored 43189 — was the app server (from the first `just serve --apps=app`, pid 39913) still running on 43189? It should have been. So isPortFree(43189) = false → allocate new → 38489. Hmm, wait, but then who is the app server now? The app dev server (from the first serve run) is still on 43189, but ports.json now says app:38489!
- cms: stored 41487 is available → but it's showing 45423?

Hmm, that doesn't add up either. Wait, let me re-read. The current state: ports.json = {app: 38489, cms: 45423, boards: 43781}.

cms2 serve reports "✓ cms ready (2m28s)", and the URL table has no "not answering" marks — meaning in that run, the cms dev server was probed and found ready. But which port? serve.mjs probes the port resolved in that run. The tail of the cms.log banner shows localhost:45423. And 45423 is now responding 200. So in the cms2 run, cms was served on 45423, not 41487.

Why 45423? Because when cms2 ran resolveDevServerPorts, the stored cms port 41487 must have failed isPortFree... or something. Actually, wait — I killed the cms serve group (42707), so 41487 should have been released... except if the kill failed to release the port. My check showed "cms port: 000 → down (as expected)". So 41487 was released.

Hmm, wait, actually — looking at the timeline more carefully:

1. `just serve --apps=app` (39913): resolveDevServerPorts → stored {43189,41487,37315} from the original just up; app:43189 available → reuse; cms:41487 available → reuse; boards:37315 available → reuse. ports.json unchanged. Serves app on 43189. ✓
2. `just serve --apps=cms` (42707): same resolution, all available → reuse. Serves cms on 41487. ✓ (confirmed 41487 200)
3. `just serve --apps=boards` (45394): resolution — app:43189 (app server running → in use), cms:41487 (cms server running → in use), boards:37315 (available → reuse?). But wait, at that point the app and cms dev servers from runs 1 and 2 were still running (I had only killed the triple-serve, not the app-only/cms-only serves). Hmm, but the boards run showed the boards build on 37315 (the tail of boards.log showed 37315? Actually, the tail of the last boards.log I looked at showed a banner... no, the earlier boards.log tail showed the network banner at 37315 — yes, "http://localhost:37315/").

But now, ports.json says boards: 43781! And app: 38489.

4. `just serve --apps=cms` (50053): resolution — stored {43189,41487,37315}: app:43189 (app running → in use → new: 38489), cms:41487 (available → reuse... but shows 45423!).

Something's inconsistent. Unless when run 4 resolved, the app server (from run 1) was also dead. Hmm, but then app would also be "available" and reused (43189), not 38489.

Wait wait. Let me re-read resolveDevServerPorts:

```js
for (const { name } of DEV_SERVERS) {
    const candidate = stored[name];
    if (Number.isInteger(candidate) && !taken.has(candidate) && (await isPortFree(candidate))) {
      ports[name] = candidate;
    } else {
      ports[name] = await allocateUnused(taken);
    }
    taken.add(ports[name]);
  }
```

For run 4: order is app, cms, boards (order of DEV_SERVERS).
- app: candidate 43189, available? The app dev server from run 1 (pid 39913) — was it still running at that point? The app serve run (39913) — did it terminate after reporting ready? `just serve` after readiness calls `finishDevServers` and waits for SIGINT/Ctrl-C or a crash. Since I kept stdin open via /dev/zero, it should keep running indefinitely...

Hmm, wait, /dev/zero is an infinite stream of NUL bytes! Not an open-but-quiet fd — it's infinite zeros. Vite/nx's CLI reads stdin and... might treat NUL bytes as input! The "press s to stop" shortcut might react to bytes. Hmm, but the earlier `just serve` (36308) with /dev/zero ran for 12+ minutes without the servers terminating. And the app serve (39913) with /dev/zero — app stayed up the whole time (I confirmed 200 multiple times across several minutes). So /dev/zero isn't killing the servers. OK.

But here's the decisive point: was run 1's `just serve` (39913) — after the app became ready — still running at the time of run 4? serve.mjs after readiness: `superviseStartup` returns, prints the URL table, then `finishDevServers` — which waits for stop signals or a crash. So yes, it stays. Unless the run 1 process got killed when I ran `kill -TERM -- -42707`? No, that's the cms serve group (42707), not the app (39913).

Hmm, wait — but now, is the app dev server still running on 43189? If the actual dev servers are now on 38489/45423/43781, the proxy will 502!

Ugh. Port re-allocation is the problem: `just serve` re-resolves all ports on each run, and if the previously stored port is in use (by a leftover server from an earlier partial run), it allocates a new port and rewrites ports.json — but the proxy's nginx conf (rendered at `just up` time with the old ports) doesn't get re-rendered. `just serve` does not re-render the nginx conf (only `just up` does). So the `just serve` after port changes breaks the proxy routing!

Hold on, is that really true? Let me check what the current nginx.conf (in .urbo/workspace/) points to. It was rendered by `just up` with the ports.json at that time (43189/41487/37315). If ports.json has since changed to 38489/45423/43781, then the proxy is still routing to 43189/41487/37315.

- cms: run 4 served on 45423 → old nginx routes to 41487 → broken
- boards: run 3 served on...? The boards.log banner showed 37315. But ports.json now says boards:43781. Did run 4's resolveDevServerPorts also re-resolve boards? So at the time of run 4: 43189 (app running), 41487 (cms running? I thought I had killed it...), 37315 (boards running) all in use → all three got new ports (38489, 45423, 43781). And cms2 (run 4) served cms on 45423.

And the boards run 3 (45394) — after reporting "not answering yet", it continued in finishDevServers (waiting). boards then became ready on 37315. That serve (45394) might still be alive holding the boards server on 37315.

OK, this is getting complicated. The current real state:
- ports.json: {app:38489, cms:45423, boards:43781} (written by run 4)
- The nginx.conf installed in the proxy was rendered by `just up` with {app:43189, cms:41487, boards:37315}
- Running dev servers: app on 43189 (run 1, probably alive), cms on 45423 (run 4), boards on 37315 (run 3), and possibly a stray app attempt on 38489? (Run 4 only serves the selected cms; the port resolution just allocates and records, and only the selected servers are served.)

- App dev server: only the one from run 1, on 43189.
- Boards dev server: only the one from run 3, on 37315.
- CMS dev server: the one from run 4, on 45423.

- boards.workspace.localhost → 37315 → boards server ✓ works
- cms.workspace.localhost → 41487 → nothing (the old cms died) ✗ broken (the new cms is on 45423)

To fix cms properly, the cleanest thing is: kill all dev-server runs and leftover servers, restore the consistency between ports.json and the rendered nginx.conf, and start all three in one `just serve` run (with all three ports free, it will reuse the stored ports, matching the nginx conf).

I need to make ports.json match the nginx conf, i.e., restore ports.json to {app:43189, cms:41487, boards:37315}. That file is in .urbo/workspace/ports.json. I can write it back. Then a single `just serve` (all three) will reuse the original ports matching the nginx conf.
